draft.title: Measures of health status
card: the average number of years a person born today could expect to live, if current death rates stay the same.
the number of deaths in a population, often given as a rate per 100,000 people so that groups of different sizes can be compared.
the amount of illness, disease or injury in a population. It counts people who are unwell, not deaths.
the number of babies who die before their first birthday, usually given per 1,000 live births.
draft.remember: Life expectancy, mortality, morbidity and infant mortality each measure a different part of a population's health.

a.q: A report counts how many people in a state were treated for asthma last year. Which measure is this?
a.why: Asthma treatment counts people who are ill, so it is morbidity. Mortality is the tempting wrong answer, but it counts deaths, not people living with illness.
a.clue: Are the people counted ill or have they died?

b.q: In Karrin Shire, 12 babies died before their first birthday, out of 4,000 live births. Which statement about this is correct?
opts: It is an infant mortality figure of 3 per 1,000 births
It is a morbidity figure of 3 per 1,000 births
It is a life expectancy figure of 12 years
It is a mortality rate of 12 per 100,000 people
b.why: Deaths of babies before age one, given per 1,000 live births, is infant mortality: 12 out of 4,000 is 3 per 1,000. The mortality option is tempting, but it uses the whole population as its base and not live births.
b.clue: Look at who died and what the figure is compared with.

b.best: It is an infant mortality figure of 3 per 1,000 births

check.summary: No problems found. The definitions are accurate, both questions have one clear right answer (12 out of 4,000 is 3 per 1,000), and the explanations agree with the card.
